opening.title: Notes from the Road
opening.body: These notes began between home and the edge of my maps. Read as yourself or someone you play. Tap a name to jump; the links below lead back.

how_to.title: A Deck in Hand
how_to.body: Use a deck to draw its top card. Sneak-use to shuffle. To return a card, hold it in your offhand and sneak-use the deck. Otherwise, keep your offhand clear while handling cards.

how_to.title: Around the Table
how_to.body: Use a loose card on a clear, flat surface to lay it face-down. Use it to flip; sneak-use to rotate. Empty-hand hit picks it up. Hit with a deck to return it; sneak-hit gathers nearby cards.

reading.title: A Little Reading
reading.body: Try one card for a choice, or three for a story. These are prompts, never predictions. Deal blind: hold a deck and aim at a table, then /trigger tarot.action set 5.

sections.title: Major Arcana
sections.intro: Turning points I have met along the road.

entries.name: The Fool
entries.body: Beyond the last path marker lay a valley missing from my map. I went down with bread and questions. For a new character, curiosity can be enough to begin.

entries.name: The Magician
entries.body: A stalled journey left me with spare planks. They became a workbench and a way onward. Ask what a character can make from the means already at hand.

entries.name: The High Priestess
entries.body: The library's quietest corner held the book everyone walked past. I stayed to read. A character may learn more by attending to a silence than filling it with an answer.

entries.name: The Empress
entries.body: Bees kept visiting the wild edge of my neat garden. I left it alone, and the whole place grew livelier. What abundance might a character welcome instead of managing away?

entries.name: The Emperor
entries.body: The keep's watchtower showed me who its gates kept waiting. Structure shapes more than a skyline. Ask whether a character's authority gives other people a secure place.

entries.name: The Hierophant
entries.body: A village taught me its way of marking safe roads. I borrowed the useful parts and asked about the rest. Which shared custom would your character learn before changing?

entries.name: The Lovers
entries.body: Our routes diverged where we had planned a home. Drawing them honestly helped us choose together. What value or affection would a character commit to?

entries.name: The Chariot
entries.body: At a rail junction, every route looked urgent until I chose a destination. Direction asks us to gather competing aims. Give a character a journey they mean to guide.

entries.name: Strength
entries.body: A shy horse watched me from the far fence. Waiting quietly was harder than approaching. Let a character discover courage through patience with what they cannot force.

entries.name: The Hermit
entries.body: I let the village lights go out before I wrote in my notebook. Without anyone to impress, I could finally ask which road I actually wanted to take.

entries.name: Wheel of Fortune
entries.body: The empty patch on my map became a busy settlement on the next visit. Places keep changing without us. How might a character respond when familiar circumstances turn?

entries.name: Justice
entries.body: Two travelers described the same dispute differently. I checked the path markers before judging. Ask what evidence a character owes the people affected by their decision.

entries.name: The Hanged Man
entries.body: Under the bridge, I noticed the bank my usual route concealed. A chosen pause can change the question. What could a character see by giving up their familiar vantage?

entries.name: Death
entries.body: I mapped the abandoned base but left its faded sign alone. A place can matter after its chapter closes. What would a character honor when it is time to leave?

entries.name: Temperance
entries.body: Where two streams met, I widened the channel a block at a time. Neither needed to disappear. I kept checking where the water went after my neat solution.

entries.name: The Devil
entries.body: I visited the treasure room so often that the road beyond it vanished from my plans. A prize became a tether. What bargain keeps a character returning despite its cost?

entries.name: The Tower
entries.body: The spire had burned when I returned; only its stone footings remained. My old map still showed its height. I kept that page, but could no longer use it as a guide.

entries.name: The Star
entries.body: Someone had set a bucket beside the repaired village well. That small sign of care outlasted my memory of the ruins. What might make a character willing to hope again?

entries.name: The Moon
entries.body: Moonlight turned a marsh pool into what looked like solid ground. I checked before stepping. Let a character hold a fear and a possibility apart until evidence arrives.

entries.name: The Sun
entries.body: We ate in the sunny courtyard and forgot to discuss our route. Delight sometimes asks only that we notice it. Give a character a moment with nothing to hide or prove.

entries.name: Judgement
entries.body: The bell called us back to a promise nobody had finished keeping. Returning meant answering honestly. Which old choice might a character be ready to judge anew?

entries.name: The World
entries.body: At last, the maps joined into one landscape, including roads I once feared. Completion deserves attention. Let a character see the whole journey before choosing the next.

sections.title: Wands
sections.intro: Bright ideas and the journeys they set in motion.

entries.name: Ace of Wands
entries.body: A torch at the edge of the clearing made an unwritten route feel possible. Inspiration needs a start. What would a character try while their interest is still warm?

entries.name: Two of Wands
entries.body: From the watchtower I could trace two journeys, but travel neither yet. Planning has its own appetite. How wide a horizon would a character choose for this undertaking?

entries.name: Three of Wands
entries.body: The boats vanished beyond the headland while I prepared for their return. A venture widens the world it touches. What new arrival could a character make ready to meet?

entries.name: Four of Wands
entries.body: The village arch was finished when I returned, with a lantern left for me. Shared milestones can make a place a home. Whose arrival would a character celebrate?

entries.name: Five of Wands
entries.body: Five travelers argued over a campsite, each noticing a different problem. Those differences mattered more than a winner. How could a character make disagreement useful?

entries.name: Six of Wands
entries.body: They hung a banner for the map I brought home. I named the guides who had kept me from getting lost. What help belongs beside a character's public success?

entries.name: Seven of Wands
entries.body: I defended the small path our map left out when a new wall threatened it. A position may be worth the effort. Which overlooked need would a character stand up for?

entries.name: Eight of Wands
entries.body: A volley of arrows sent us moving before our discussion was done. Some scenes gather speed all at once. What message or decision needs a character's attention right now?

entries.name: Nine of Wands
entries.body: At the repaired fence, the watchkeeper knew every mark and barely sat down. Endurance has a cost. Who could help a character keep a boundary without bearing it alone?

entries.name: Ten of Wands
entries.body: I packed supplies for every imagined problem and could hardly reach the dock. Preparation had become a burden. What could a character entrust to a companion instead?

entries.name: Page of Wands
entries.body: A biome I had never drawn filled three notebook pages. New interests can stay exploratory. What would a character investigate without promising to become an expert?

entries.name: Knight of Wands
entries.body: The next hill kept pulling me beyond the route I'd planned. Restless courage can discover much and finish little. What would persuade a character to stop and stay?

entries.name: Queen of Wands
entries.body: The host hung their brightest banner despite the neighbors' jokes. By supper I had unrolled my own odd sketch. Their confidence made trying feel possible.

entries.name: King of Wands
entries.body: A settlement plan changed when I walked it with future neighbors. Vision needs people as well as distance. What direction could a character help others make their own?

sections.title: Cups
sections.intro: Feelings, friendships and the places that become dear to us.

entries.name: Ace of Cups
entries.body: A spring beside the path caught the sky so clearly that I stopped drawing. Wonder can arrive before an explanation. What new feeling could your character allow to begin?

entries.name: Two of Cups
entries.body: A traveler offered half the campfire, and I offered half my supper. Neither offer needed a tally. Let two characters recognize each other through shared kindness.

entries.name: Three of Cups
entries.body: Three friends brought food and stories from different roads. For once, I had no wish to be elsewhere. Who gives a character the easy joy of being among their people?

entries.name: Four of Cups
entries.body: I stared across the pond while someone offered me a bowl. My thoughts had made the present almost invisible. What invitation might a withdrawn character fail to notice?

entries.name: Five of Cups
entries.body: The flood erased the trail I loved, though the crossing farther up survived. Loss needn't hide what remains. Let a character notice both without hurrying into gratitude.

entries.name: Six of Cups
entries.body: The treehouse sign still spelled our grand plans badly. I remembered our kindness toward those plans. What joy could a character revisit without moving into the past?

entries.name: Seven of Cups
entries.body: In the market, every stall suggested a life I could lead. Choosing felt harder than imagining. Ask which desire a character can name once the alternatives fall quiet.

entries.name: Eight of Cups
entries.body: I left a safe harbor once my questions outgrew its walls. Affection did not make staying right. What valued place might a character need to leave without blaming it?

entries.name: Nine of Cups
entries.body: My favorite supper tasted best after I stopped planning the next journey. A private wish had come true in a small way. What would let a character enjoy having enough?

entries.name: Ten of Cups
entries.body: The feast stretched down the street, with a place saved for late arrivals. Happiness became a shared practice. What does a character do to help that welcome continue?

entries.name: Page of Cups
entries.body: A fish stole the center of my pond sketch. I sent the crooked drawing to someone I missed; it said more than the careful letter I had put aside.

entries.name: Knight of Cups
entries.body: I carried flowers across three biomes before daring to offer them. A beautiful intention needs room for a reply. What invitation could a character make without presuming?

entries.name: Queen of Cups
entries.body: At the window seat, my friend heard what I hadn't mapped. They did not press when I fell quiet. I left knowing I could return to the unfinished story.

entries.name: King of Cups
entries.body: The harbor keeper heard our quarrel without borrowing our anger. Later, alone by the water, they admitted how much it had cost to answer steadily.

sections.title: Swords
sections.intro: Questions, difficult truths and the limits of a first impression.

entries.name: Ace of Swords
entries.body: A clear footprint settled the question our guesses had tangled. Truth can be simple without being easy. What plain observation would change a character's understanding?

entries.name: Two of Swords
entries.body: I kept two routes folded shut because choosing would disappoint someone. Waiting began to choose for me. What feeling or fact must a character admit to break a stalemate?

entries.name: Three of Swords
entries.body: A broken sign told me more about the quarrel than the cheerful village map. Some truths hurt to read. Let a story make room for sorrow without explaining it away.

entries.name: Four of Swords
entries.body: I left my armor by the bed, but kept unfolding the map. My body had stopped before my mind would. That evening I learned how hard a real pause could be.

entries.name: Five of Swords
entries.body: The victor described the quarrel while everyone else left the arena. Being right had become a lonely prize. What would a character lose by insisting on the final word?

entries.name: Six of Swords
entries.body: We crossed the river with old worries beside our tools. The farther bank offered room, not forgetfulness. Let a character begin moving before their feelings catch up.

entries.name: Seven of Swords
entries.body: A hidden tunnel shortened my route and left the gatekeeper misinformed. An elegant plan can conceal its price. Who needs to know what a character has chosen not to say?

entries.name: Eight of Swords
entries.body: The fence maze had openings I could not reach alone. A companion found a loose panel. I had mistaken needing help for having no way out.

entries.name: Nine of Swords
entries.body: At midnight I drew dangers onto tomorrow's route. My companion could not promise safety, but stayed while I named them. The map was still there at dawn.

entries.name: Ten of Swords
entries.body: The outpost marked on my map no longer existed. At last I stopped planning around its return. A story can acknowledge a final defeat and begin the next page elsewhere.

entries.name: Page of Swords
entries.body: I noted the strange tracks before deciding what had made them. Curiosity needs a little discipline. Which suspicion could a character turn into a testable question?

entries.name: Knight of Swords
entries.body: I hurried home with a theory and nearly missed the witness who could correct it. Urgency can narrow a good mind. Who should a character hear before charging ahead?

entries.name: Queen of Swords
entries.body: The judge let the silence last until I stopped dressing my excuse as an explanation. I dreaded her next question, and trusted her more for asking it.

entries.name: King of Swords
entries.body: The council compared maps, heard objections and gave its reasons. Authority makes its thinking visible. What principle would a character defend when it limits them too?

sections.title: Pentacles
sections.intro: Resources, learned skills and things worth tending between journeys.

entries.name: Ace of Pentacles
entries.body: A traveler gave me a seed from a place I wanted to understand. I planted it before planning a garden. What modest opportunity could a character turn into patient action?

entries.name: Two of Pentacles
entries.body: Two furnaces and changing fuel taught me to adjust my pace. Balance moves as its demands do. How could a character keep two needs in view and respond to both?

entries.name: Three of Pentacles
entries.body: The mason knew the stone, the carpenter its frame; I mapped the approach. I kept offering answers until I noticed nobody had asked me to solve their part.

entries.name: Four of Pentacles
entries.body: The locked storeroom was full while the shared workshop lacked tools. Security had stopped serving its purpose. What would a character fear if they loosened their grip?

entries.name: Five of Pentacles
entries.body: I once passed a warm doorway because I thought the welcome belonged to others. Need can make a place seem closed. Who could help a character find a practical way inside?

entries.name: Six of Pentacles
entries.body: The supply chest let me choose what I lacked instead of proving I deserved it. Help has terms, even unspoken ones. What would make a character's generosity respectful?

entries.name: Seven of Pentacles
entries.body: The orchard bore less than I had hoped. I walked each row before packing up. Was I waiting for growth, or reluctant to admit I wanted to leave?

entries.name: Eight of Pentacles
entries.body: I drew the same shoreline until my hand noticed details I had missed. Practice changes attention. What small correction could help a character grow into their craft?

entries.name: Nine of Pentacles
entries.body: The garden I tended between journeys had become worth staying in. Independence includes enjoying its fruits. Let a character appreciate a comfort they can sustain.

entries.name: Ten of Pentacles
entries.body: New arrivals used old maps to extend the village paths. An inheritance stays alive through use. What could a character leave that gives the next people a beginning?

entries.name: Page of Pentacles
entries.body: A new sapling became an experiment by my door. Learning sometimes needs a small patch of ground. What practical interest could a character give steady attention?

entries.name: Knight of Pentacles
entries.body: The farmer checked each gate and showed me a latch that saved a trip. Reliability can learn. What routine could a character improve while keeping its quiet promise?

entries.name: Queen of Pentacles
entries.body: A kitchen offered dry boots and a chair without asking for my story. I had come prepared to explain why I needed help. For once, I could just sit down.

entries.name: King of Pentacles
entries.body: The granary keeper knew which stores the village could spare and which it needed. Security asks for judgment. What resource could a character steward for others?

sections.title: The Digits
sections.intro: Nine number characters to try beside a scene or a question.

entries.name: One
entries.body: I placed one marker beyond the last known trail and called it a beginning. One gives initiative a voice. What could a character choose without waiting for someone else?

entries.name: Two
entries.body: Two maps disagreed until their makers compared the ground between them. Partnership needs both accounts. How could a character hear another voice while keeping their own?

entries.name: Three
entries.body: Three colors made the route banner easier to share than my explanation. Expression can invite company. What idea might a character discover by saying it aloud to someone?

entries.name: Four
entries.body: Four corner posts turned a stopping place into a reliable shelter. Structure can make freedom easier to live with. What steady habit helps a character keep what matters?

entries.name: Five
entries.body: The branching trail took me beyond my map. I loved having no fixed route, until I noticed how often I left just as a place began to know me.

entries.name: Six
entries.body: At supper I noticed the host had served everyone but themselves. Care needs room for its giver too. How could a character look after the one holding a home together?

entries.name: Seven
entries.body: I stayed by the cave wall until I noticed its pattern. Seven values inward attention. What question could a character consider quietly before seeking company?

entries.name: Eight
entries.body: The trading hall's neat rows hid how its keeper shaped our days. Eight gives power a practical form. What consequences should a character count besides their own gain?

entries.name: Nine
entries.body: Before leaving, I copied my maps for travelers I would never meet. Nine gives completion a wider reach. What could a character release without seeing who takes it?

sections.title: Master Numbers
sections.intro: Modern numerology motifs: closer attention, wider building and shared care.

entries.name: Eleven
entries.body: Two listeners noticed a pause between tunnel sounds. Eleven heightens Two's attention. Let an impression lead a character to ask and check before declaring an answer.

entries.name: Twenty-Two
entries.body: The long bridge joined villages once far apart on my map. Twenty-Two widens Four's foundations. What lasting work could a character make useful beyond their own circle?

entries.name: Thirty-Three
entries.body: At the workshop, I shared a route and learned a better knot. Thirty-Three widens Six through teaching. Care can travel both ways and leave time for the teacher's road.

closer.title: Leave a Light On
closer.body: Map folded, cards tucked away, and someone has saved me a chair. The rest can wait till tomorrow. A good road should have a welcome at its end.
